article.title: WATCH: Andy Burnham's 'enormous black hole' in Britain's finances analysed by Olivia Utley
article.summary: GB News Political Correspondent Olivia Utley discusses Andy Burnham ruling out a snap election and how the PM could benefit from a new manifesto.Speaking to host Dawn Neesom, Olivia said: "Andy Burnham has an enormous black hole in the country's finances, £5billion on defence alone. Obviously, the global pressures have changed dramatically since 2024, thanks to the war in Iran pushing up our energy prices, and Andy Burnham has made it pretty clear he's not going to reform welfare."That would be an easy way of getting money quickly. The only other easy way of getting money quickly, because the Government doesn't seem to have a sort of serious growth agenda at the moment. The only other way to get money quickly is to raise taxes on working people."He can't do that because of that manifesto. Will he find that in a few months time, he feels he has to call in a general election to get his own mandate."WATCH ABOVE.Our Standards:The GB News Editorial Charter

article.title: Andy Burnham hints at tax rises under Labour plan to fund adult social care
article.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has conceded that his landmark pledge to transform social care in England will not materialise during the current parliament, instead deferring the overhaul to Labour's manifesto for the 2029 general election.The admission marks a significant retreat from the ambitions Mr Burnham expressed upon taking the Labour leadership in July, when he vowed to spend "whatever political capital I have" on repairing Britain's struggling care system.Labour now intends to campaign at the next election on a specific plan to fund a care system that would be free at the point of use, financed through dedicated tax rises.Mr Burnham acknowledged that existing commitments in Labour's current manifesto constrain his ability to act before the next election.Speaking to BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, he said: "I have to keep people's trust as well, and there are commitments in the manifesto that would make it hard to do in this Parliament."Rather than pressing ahead now, the Prime Minist...

article.title: WATCH: Andy Burnham promises a 'new direction' for Britain as he arrives at his first Labour conference as PM
article.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has promised to take Britain in a "new direction" as he arrives in Liverpool for his first Labour Party conference as PM.Speaking to the crowd, Mr Burnham said: "I will set out a clear new direction for the country, and from that comes the hope, people able to have hope again, that things will improve, that life will get better, and it will."You can see the change in this city led by Mayor Steve Rotherham. It's brilliant, isn't it? You see what's happening. Wonderful to see Liverpool growing faster than the rest of the UK economy. How many times in our lifetimes have we been able to say that?"But we'll set out a plan to get that growth going right around the country. Good growth in every postcode, hope in every heart. That's what the Labour Party under my leadership will be all about. It's wonderful to be in Liverpool with you all and we're going to have a great week."WATCH ABOVE.Our Standards:The GB News Editorial Charter
